subject: Film & Cinema
title: Soviet and Eastern European Animation
description: A quick, practical guide to Soviet and Eastern European Animation.

hook.text: Behind the Iron Curtain, animators made some of the most experimental and beautiful films ever.

buildup.text: Soviet animation used allegory to smuggle political commentary past censors.

discovery.text: Yuri Norstein's Hedgehog in the Fog is considered one of the greatest animated films ever made.

twist.text: Most Western audiences have never seen these films — a treasure trove hidden by language and politics.

climax.text: Eastern European animation proves that great art flourishes even under restriction.

punchline.text: The most controlled societies made the freest animation.

quiz.question: Why was Soviet animation often allegorical?
options: To smuggle political commentary past state censors
